description.narrative: thousands of houses have been destroyed and several villages submerged after flooding triggered by torrential rainfall killed 100 people across Sudan, according to an aid group in the country. thousands of people in the impoverished eastern region bordering Eritrea were forced to flee after the river Gash burst its banks, flooding entire villages inhabited by farmers. The affected population have lost their house, livestock and shelter they live on the open ground without any means of protection and are at exposure of many risks threatening their lives including outbreak of Malaria and other related diseases they are in need of shelters and mosquito nets to protect themselves from Malaria which is common in the area. CAFOD with its partner SIDO plan to target 500 families in Eljablaian and Rabat localities it’s expected to be very smooth process for CAFOD and its partner as they have been involved in White Nile state since 2014 responding the South Sudanese refugee’s crises. 500 families will be targeted each one of them will receive a package of 2 Blanket, 6 pieces of soaps, 2 Jerry-cans, 3 Mosquito net, plastic sheet and 2 matts. The quicker the response the better as the risk to their well-being will be reduced. According the assessment conducted these are the top priority needs for the affected people these items would help the people to survive in this year. So far only Plan international has provided 250 plastic sheets and 800 matt which is not enough and might only cover 200 families out of 1660.
